long_biography.plain_text:
Mas entered the family business through MasTec, where he led international operations and a construction division. In 2002 he became chief executive of Neff, then one of the country’s largest equipment rental companies. He sold his Neff shares and stepped down as chief executive in 2007, later leaving its board.

After Neff, Mas established the Mas Group and founded Synergy Rents, returning to equipment rental as a founder. The portfolio expanded into Bobcat dealerships, infrastructure suppliers, healthcare investments and Florida property development. More recently, a Mas controlled company has advanced a large mixed use industrial project near Miami Gardens, while Synergy remains an active county equipment rental vendor.

uncertainties: No dedicated Forbes.com profile was found. A Forbes article calls Juan Carlos Mas a construction magnate in vessel coverage, but the article is used only as an identity cross-check and is not treated as a profile or as business-history evidence.

Juan Carlos Mas is a common name with dozens of LinkedIn results across several countries. Doctors, energy professionals, Spanish executives and other namesakes were rejected. The target is resolved by the combined Miami and Coral Gables geography, brother relationships to Jorge and José Mas, MasTec and Neff history, Mas Group and Synergy roles, and Nicklaus Children's connection.
The immutable vessel relationships were used only as identity context. Vessel names, ownership, values, locations and dimensions are excluded from both biographies and all wealth classifications.

The immutable record gives United States birth country and American nationality. A 2002 proxy says Mas was 35 but does not establish an exact birth date or place. No birth-day, month, year or birthplace proposal is made, and Cuban family heritage is not converted into Cuban citizenship.

No personal LinkedIn URL could be distinguished confidently from the many namesakes, and no verified personal Instagram or standalone personal website was found. Only the official Synergy Company Website is proposed.

The brothers bought a large MasTec partnership stake from a trust established under their father's will in 1998, and Juan Carlos also worked actively in the business. The public filing does not disclose the purchase terms or his individual economic share, so the stake is evidence of a material family platform but not described as a simple inheritance.

Mas served as Neff shareholder, chief executive and chairman, sold his shares and resigned as chief executive in May 2007, and left the board in 2010. Neff is historical rather than a current holding, and no later United Rentals acquisition value is attributed personally to him.

Synergy's official site says the business was founded in 2012, while securities and Florida entity records place Mas's founder-chair tenure or legal formation in 2013. The biographies avoid a precise founding year; both timelines support the durable founder relationship.

The official Synergy site describes an August 2024 merger with Opifex. It does not disclose Mas's post-merger equity percentage, so the dossier retains his independently documented founder-chair relationship without claiming full ownership or assigning the combined fleet and branches to him personally.

A MasTec 2026 filing says the CCI ownership interests were sold during the first quarter and the related-party relationship ended. CCI is therefore not presented as a current holding or role even though Mas had served as its chairman.

Miami-Dade records identify Mas as owner and managing member of seven Bobcat dealers and sole owner of MASCAP Qualified Opportunity Fund. Individual dealership inventory, Synergy equipment, operating branches and project-vehicle assets remain company property rather than directly held personal assets.

The Miami Gardens development is a proposed, phased company project. Headline development cost, land area, prospective buildings and future jobs are not counted as completed assets, personal wealth or current operating results.

MasTec filings distinguish Jorge and José Mas's football-franchise and aircraft-leasing interests from Juan Carlos Mas. Those brothers' assets and activities are not attributed to the target; trust roles likewise do not establish Juan Carlos's beneficial ownership of trust assets.

The Mixed origin classification reflects two documented mechanisms: family-company equity and access, and separately founded or controlled later ventures. Public evidence does not quantify which mechanism now contributes more, so Inherited, Inherited and expanded, or Self-made — advantaged start alone would overstate the available evidence.

Blank title, suffix, secondary nationality, secondary residence, birth, death, age, internal-note and unknown-name fields remain unsupported, optional, inapplicable or system-managed rather than enrichment targets.
